text_blocks.snippet: Yes, standard homeowners insurance in Utah generally covers hail damage to your home—including roofs, siding, gutters, and windows—as long as it is caused by a sudden, accidental storm and you pay your deductible.
However, how much your insurer actually pays out depends on your specific policy terms:
Key Factors That Affect Your Payout

list.snippet: Replacement Cost Value (RCV) vs. Actual Cash Value (ACV): RCV covers the cost to repair or replace damaged materials at today's prices (often paid in two steps: an initial payment minus depreciation and deductible, then the remaining recoverable depreciation once repairs are finished). ACV subtracts depreciation for your roof's age and wear, which can leave you paying a large share out of pocket on an older roof .

Deductibles (Flat vs. Percentage): Check your declarations page for both your standard deductible and any separate wind/hail deductible. Percentage deductibles (often 1% to 5%) are typically calculated based on your home's dwelling coverage limit—not the repair cost . Under Utah law, contractors cannot legally waive or absorb your deductible.

Roof Schedules & Cosmetic Exclusions: Some policies use roof payment schedules that reduce payouts based on roof age, or include cosmetic exclusions (commonly on metal roofs) if hail only causes surface dents without affecting function.

Utah Matching Rule: Under Utah insurance rules (Utah Admin. Code R590-190-13), if you have replacement cost coverage and repairs leave materials mismatched in appearance, your insurer generally must address uniform appearance for covered exterior or interior losses, minus your deductible.

text_blocks.snippet: For official policy questions or consumer help in the state, you can check resources from the Utah Insurance Department , and Coverage Classroom also breaks down Utah claim timelines and rules.
If you want to estimate what a claim might look like for your home, share your deductible (flat dollar or percentage), whether your policy is RCV or ACV, and roughly how old your roof is.
